title: Campfire all-hands slate and exec brief v0.1
content:
Purpose / context:

This is the working slate for the upcoming company-wide all-hands (internal name: CAMPFIRE). Primary goals: calibrate exec priorities with the org, surface cross-team risks ahead of Q2 sprint kickoffs, and publish a compact set of company-level OKRs for feedback before finalization. Treat this doc as an iterative run-card: short, conversational, and anchored to a 30–45 minute run-of-show plus a 20-minute breakout / AMA window.

High-level framing (one-liner for slides):
"Redwood in 1: Focused reliability, pragmatic cost wins, and defensible private deployments — shipped and observable."

Proposed company OKRs (draft, for discussion):
- OKR 1: Production predictability and SLOs.
  - KR1.1: Reduce 95th-percentile hosted API request latency by 20% on common gen workloads (baseline: 420ms).
  - KR1.2: Increase Dedicated SLA attainment to 99.8% (monthly rolling).
  - KR1.3: Ship KV-cache diagnostics and reduce cache-miss tail by 30%.
  - Rationale: reliability is our top enterprise ask and the leading driver of deal progression for Dedicated/Private.

- OKR 2: Unit-cost efficiency and footprint.
  - KR2.1: Lower per-token inference cost of our top-5 workloads by 18% through batching + quantization profiles.
  - KR2.2: Pilot on-prem quantized runtime with two enterprise customers and capture 1 customer-ready case study.
  - KR2.3: Roll out automated batching suggestions in Console to 50% of active teams.
  - Rationale: cost controls improve both gross margin and net-new adoption by enabling lower-priced SLAs.

- OKR 3: Product velocity and developer experience.
  - KR3.1: Ship function-calling stable SDK with three major integrations (node, python, go).
  - KR3.2: Reduce average time-to-first-successful-call for new signups from 2.6 hours to <90 minutes (instrumented funnel).
  - KR3.3: Launch 5 evaluation templates (e.g., semantic-search, code-assist) with built-in regression checks.
  - Rationale: lower friction for new product usage helps PLG funnel and reduces rate of stalled POCs.

Alignment map: what to call out in the exec update (one-paragraph bullets per product area):
- Hosted API: metrics to show — latency percentiles (p50/p95), error budget burn this quarter, top 10 routes by traffic. Callout: planned kernel switching experiment and expected latency curve.
- Dedicated: deployment adoption pipeline — commercial onboards, capacity ramp, and 2-week SLA incidents with root cause notes. Ask: confirmation on pricing tier refresh by billing.
- Private: progress on VPC onboarding, KMS/HSM integrations, regulatory checklist statuses for two pilot customers. Risk: on-prem packaging timeline slip by 3 weeks.
- Console / Rollouts: rollout UX improvements, canary instrumentation, and cost/latency per-token analytics. Ask: product marketing for the new dashboards.
- Optimize: concrete examples of batching/recommendation impact and the first customer-facing cost-savings dashboard.

Run of show (45 minutes recommended):
- 0:00–0:05 Welcome + framing by CEO (what to expect from this all-hands).
- 0:05–0:12 Exec update snapshot (CTO + Head of Product) — one slide each: reliability, cost, platform launches.
- 0:12–0:22 OKR walk-through and ask for alignment (CPO) — present the three proposed company OKRs and key KRs.
- 0:22–0:28 Customer story / case study (internal rehearsal version) — short video or recorded interview with pilot customer on Dedicated.
- 0:28–0:35 Product demos (two quick demos): batching suggestions in Console; function-calling SDK.
- 0:35–0:45 Roadmap/operational asks + closing (coordinator lists cross-team action items).
- 0:45–1:05 Breakouts + AMA (channel-based Q&A to Slack thread and live upvoted questions).

Speaker notes + concise talking points: (one-liners to paste into slide notes)
- CEO: ‘‘We’re doubling down on reliability and cost — we know customers choose reliability over experimental model bells and whistles.’’
- CTO: ‘‘This quarter’s wins will be measured by fewer incidents and more predictable tail latency — specific engineering bets are listed on the linked runbook.’’
- Head of Product: ‘‘OKRs are intentionally narrow: shipping systems that make inference predictable and cheaper for customers at scale.’’

Pre-read (to be sent 72 hours before):
- 2-page exec summary (1x page metrics, 1x page OKR descriptions).
- Short product note: what batching/quantization does for typical LLM workloads (one pager).
- Incident highlight: root cause + remediation from most recent Dedicated SLA event.

Suggested slides (10–12 slides total):
1. Title + one-line framing.
2. Company snapshot (top-line metrics: MRR, active API keys, avg latency, cost per token trend).
3. Customer highlight (quote + impact).
4. OKR overview (three objectives only).
5–7. KR detail (one slide per OKR with measurable KRs).
8. Product highlights (Console, Dedicated, Private wins).
9. Roadmap and asks.
10. Operational changes + SRE playbook updates.
11. Q&A / how to participate.
12. Next steps + links.

Communication timeline:
- D-7: Draft pre-read to execs for editing.
- D-3: Pre-read distributed to company + Slack AMA thread created.
- D-0: All-hands. Live pulse survey at D+0 + 24-hour follow-up.
- D+3: Final OKR post with consolidated feedback and owners assigned.

Pulse survey (3 quick questions asked live):
1) Is the company focus clear for the coming quarter? (Yes/No/Unsure)
2) Which objective worries you most? (free text)
3) What is one small change that would help your team achieve these KRs? (free text)

Contingency and fallback plans (short):
- If latency experiment delays: push the latency KR timeline and convert the influencing work into a clear mitigations KR (e.g., cache improv + fallback routing).
- If Dedicated SLA falls short during the commit review: engage dedicated sales + support to provide temporary credit and an incident postmortem package for affected customers.
- If pre-read engagement is low: schedule 15-minute team-level syncs with product leads to run the pre-read highlights.

Open questions / unresolved items (for discussion with execs):
- Final numeric targets for KR1.1 and KR2.1 need calibration from infra cost model (Diego).
- Confirmation of two pilot customers for on-prem quantized runtime (sales to confirm by D-3).
- Do we want to add a people goal (hiring/retention) as a separate OKR or keep people goals at org-level?

Action items (initial owners):
- Samira: prepare the 1-page product explainer on batching + quantization (due D-6).
- Diego: produce an infra cost sensitivity table with scenarios for KR2.1 (due D-4).
- Priya: coordinate customer case recording and consent (due D-5).
- Avery: finalize slide deck and run-of-show and send pre-read on D-3.

Notes to deck designers and comms: keep language simple, avoid model-spec name-drops in the public pre-read, focus on customer outcomes, and ensure any customer logos have explicit permissions.

Quick scribbles / rough ideas for breakout prompts (used to guide small-group chats at D+0):
- Where are the top three friction points in current developer onboarding?
- Which product features materially reduce customer unit cost?
- What operational metrics should be visible in team dashboards to prevent incidents?

This doc is a working draft — add comments inline rather than editing the top-level OKR blurbs until we converge with execs.

Unedited margin notes:
- Consider a short internal blog post from the CEO the Monday after to capture momentum.
- Try a focused pilot: one-week battleground to reduce tail-latency for p95 on the top 2% of routes.
